verses.zh: （大卫的记念诗。）耶和华啊，求你不要在怒中责备我，不要在烈怒中惩罚我！
verses.en: A psalm of David, written to get God’s attention.[NOTE:1] O Lord, do not continue to rebuke me in your anger.Do not continue to punish me in your raging fury.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 38. The author asks the Lord to deliver him from his enemies. He confesses his sin and recognizes that the crisis he faces is the result of divine discipline. Yet he begs the Lord not to reject him.

The Hebrew text reads simply, “to cause to remember.” The same form, the Hiphil infinitive of זָכַר (zakhar, “remember”), also appears in the heading of Ps 70. Some understand this in the sense of “for the memorial offering,” but it may carry the idea of bringing one’s plight to God’s attention (see P. C. Craigie, Psalms 1-50 [WBC], 303).
verses.commentary:
38:1-8 Most other English translations have this section broken down into
several strophes. Strophe division is not a textual issue. It is speculation based on the SUBJECT
being addressed, not inspiration.

The psalmist describes his condition and feelings.

- he senses YHWH's displeasure

- do not rebuke me in Your wrath – BDB 406, KB 410, Hiphil imperfect
used in a jussive sense, cf. Ps. 6:1

- do not chasten me in Your burning anger – BDB 415, KB 418, Piel imperfect
used in a jussive sense; this verb often is used
of covenant violations (cf. Lev. 26:18,28; Ps. 6:1; 39:11; 94:10; 118:18; Hos. 10:10)

- he feels YHWH's punishment

- Your arrows have sunk deep into me, cf. Deut. 32:23; Job 6:4; Ps. 7:12-13; 45:5

- Your hand has pressed me down, cf. Ps. 32:4; 39:10 (note same verb
in both lines but used in different senses, BDB 639, KB 692)

- the physical result of YHWH's displeasure (because of sin, Ps. 38:3b,4,5b)

- no soundness (BDB 1022, shalom; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE [OT]) in my flesh

- no health in my bones

- wounds (lit. "stripes," BDB 289) grow foul (BDB 92, KB 107, Hiphil
perfect) and fester (BDB 596, KB 583, Qal
perfect)

- bent over ("bent," BDB 730, KB 796, Niphal perfect;
"bowed down," BDB 1005, KB 1458, Qal perfect,
cf. Ps. 35:14) in mourning

- loins are filled (BDB 569, KB 583, Qal perfect) with burning

- repeat of a. above

- benumbed (BDB 806, KB 916, Niphal perfect, lit. "spent")

- crushed (BDB 194, KB 221, Niphal perfect, Piel in Ps. 51:8)

- groan (BDB 980, KB 1367, Qal perfect, i.e., animal sounds)

Notice the string of perfect tense verbs.
YHWH's "anger" (BDB 893) and "wrath" (BDB 409) have
come (imperfects) and remain (perfects)! What a terrible condition of mind (Ps. 38:4,
8b) and body (cf. Psalm 32; 51)!

38:1 "burning anger" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

verses.zh: 因为，你的箭射入我身；你的手压住我。
verses.en: For your arrows pierce[NOTE:1] me,and your hand presses me down.[NOTE:2]
notes: Cf. Ps 38:1 with Ps 6:1, which has similar wording.tn The words “continue to” are supplied in the translation of both lines. The following verses make it clear that the psalmist is already experiencing divine rebuke/punishment. He asks that it might cease.

The verb Hebrew נָחַת (nakhat) apparently here means “penetrate, pierce” (note the use of the Qal in Prov 17:10). The psalmist pictures the Lord as a warrior who shoots arrows at him (see Ps 7:12-13).

verses.zh: 因你的恼怒，我的肉无一完全；因我的罪过，我的骨头也不安宁。
verses.en: My whole body is sick because of your judgment;[NOTE:1] I am deprived of health because of my sin.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and your hand [?] upon me.” The meaning of the verb נָחַת (nakhat) is unclear in this context. It could mean “your hand comes down on me.” It may be preferable to emend the form to וַתָּנַח (vattanakh) from the verb נוּחַ (nuakh, “rest”). In this case the text would read literally, “and your hand rests upon me” (see Isa 25:10, though the phrase is used in a positive sense there, unlike Ps 38:2).
Heb “there is no soundness in my flesh from before your anger.” “Anger” here refers metonymically to divine judgment, which is the practical effect of God’s anger at the psalmist’s sin.

verses.zh: 我的罪孽高过我的头，如同重担叫我担当不起。
verses.en: For my sins overwhelm me;[NOTE:1] like a heavy load, they are too much for me to bear.
notes: Heb “there is no health in my bones from before my sin.”
verses.commentary:
38:4 "over my head" This verb (BDB 716, KB 778, Qal
perfect) is used of water.

- flood as war – Isa. 8:8; 23:10; Dan. 11:10,40; Nahum 1:8

- waves – literal in Isa. 54:9

- waves – figurative of problems and emotions – Ps. 42:7; 88:16-17; 124:4-5

The psalmist's guilt from sin has overwhelmed him!

verses.zh: 因我的愚昧，我的伤发臭流脓。
verses.en: My wounds[NOTE:1] are infected and starting to smell,[NOTE:2] because of my foolish sins.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “pass over my head.”
The reference to wounds may be an extension of the metaphorical language of v. 2. The psalmist pictures himself as one whose flesh is ripped and torn by arrows.
Heb “my wounds stink, they are festering” (cf. NEB).
verses.commentary:
38:5 "fester" This verb (BDB 596, KB 628, Niphal
perfect) is used in Leviticus 26, the cursing and blessing passage parallel
to Deuteronomy 27-28. It denoted a "rotten decay" (cf. Lev. 26:39 [twice]). Sin destroys! Often
in horrible ways!

verses.zh: 我疼痛，大大拳曲，终日哀痛。
verses.en: I am dazed[NOTE:1] and completely humiliated;[NOTE:2] all day long I walk around mourning.
notes: Heb “from before my foolishness.”

The verb’s precise shade of meaning in this context is not entirely clear. The verb, which literally means “to bend,” may refer to the psalmist’s posture. In Isa 21:3 it seems to mean “be confused, dazed.”
verses.commentary:
38:6 "mourning" This term is from the Hebrew root "to be dark" (BDB 871).
It could mean

- dressed in dark clothing as a sign of mourning

- dirt placed on head and clothing as a sign of mourning

- an idiom for the condition of the heart, soul, mind (here because of known sin)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

▣ "I am bent over and greatly bowed down"
There are two parallel verbs.

- bent over – BDB 730, KB 796, Niphal perfect
which can be viewed as

- bewilderment – Isa. 21:3

- perversion of mind – 1 Sam.20:30; Prov. 12:8

- literal – which matches the parallel verb

- bowed down – BDB 1005, KB 1458, Qal perfect
which seems to denote a bent body as a figure of a bent heart

verses.zh: 我满腰是火；我的肉无一完全。
verses.en: For I am overcome with shame,[NOTE:1] and my whole body is sick.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I am bowed down to excess.”

Heb “for my loins are filled with shame.” The “loins” are viewed here as the seat of the psalmist’s emotions. The present translation assumes that נִקְלֶה (niqleh) is derived from קָלָה (qalah, “be dishonored”). Some derive it instead from a homonymic root קָלָה (qalah), meaning “to roast.” In this case one might translate “fever” (cf. NEB “my loins burn with fever”).
verses.commentary:
38:7 "loins" There are several
terms that are used in the OT to represent the whole person.

- soul – BDB 659, nephesh (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH)

- spirit – BDB 924, ruah (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE)

- heart – BDB 524, leb (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART)

- kidneys – BDB 480 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: INWARD PARTS)

- only here, loins – BDB 492

There are several more. Only context can determine when this concept is
meant. One part of the body represents the whole person.

verses.zh: 我被压伤，身体疲倦；因心里不安，我就唉哼。
verses.en: I am numb with pain and severely battered;[NOTE:1] I groan loudly because of the anxiety I feel.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “there is no soundness in my flesh” (see v. 3).
Heb “I am numb and crushed to excess.”

verses.zh: 主啊，我的心愿都在你面前；我的叹息不向你隐瞒。
verses.en: O Lord, you understand my heart’s desire;[NOTE:1] my groaning is not hidden from you.
notes: Heb “I roar because of the moaning of my heart.”
verses.commentary:
38:9-12 This strophe also describes the author's terrible condition.

- his condition

- his desire (i.e. prayer) is before YHWH (i.e., for forgiveness and restoration of fellowship)

- his sighing is known to YHWH, cf. Ps. 31:10

- his physical condition

- heart throbs – BDB 695, KB 749, Niphal perfect

- strength fails – BDB 736, KB 806, Qal perfect

- eyes fail –no verbs; this is not referring to blindness but
is an idiom for the lack of health, joy, peace, cf. Ps. 13:3; 1 Sam.14:29; Ezra 9:8

- interpersonal issues

- loved ones stand aloof

- friends stand aloof

- kinsmen stand far off

- enemies seek his death

(1) lay snares

(2) threaten destruction

(3) devise treachery all day long; the verb BDB 211,
KB 237, is lit. "groan." The psalmist "groans" (BDB 980, Ps. 38:8) but the
wicked "devise" (cf. Prov. 24:2).

verses.zh: 我心跳动，我力衰微，连我眼中的光也没有了。
verses.en: My heart beats quickly;my strength leaves me.I can hardly see.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “O Lord, before you [is] all my desire.”

verses.zh: 我的良朋密友因我的灾病都躲在旁边站着；我的亲戚本家也远远地站立。
verses.en: Because of my condition,[NOTE:1] even my friends and acquaintances keep their distance;[NOTE:2] my neighbors stand far away.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and the light of my eyes, even they, there is not with me.” The “light of the eyes” may refer to physical energy (see 1 Sam 14:27, 29), life itself (Ps 13:3), or the ability to see (Prov 29:23).
Or “wound,” or “illness.”
Heb “stand [aloof].”
verses.commentary:
38:11

NASB, NKJV
"plague"

NKJV, JPSOA
"affliction"

TEV
"sores"

NJB
"disease"

REB
"sickness"

Peshitta
"grief"

The word (BDB 619) means "stroke/wound," "plague," or "mark."

- plague – cf. Gen. 12:17; Exod. 11:1; 1 Kgs. 8:37-38; 2 Chr. 6:28-29; Ps. 39:10; 91:10

- leprosy (OT sense) – Leviticus 13-14; Deut. 24:8

- wound – Deut. 17:8; 21:5; Isa. 53:8

- discipline (for children) – 2 Sam. 7:14; Ps. 89:32; Prov. 6:23

Most words have multiple usages or else human vocabulary would be
impossible to know and use. When an interpreter comes to a context, they
seek the meaning intended by the original author and understandable to the
hearers/readers of that day. This context is a divinely given physical
manifestation of His displeasure over human sin. The punishment is meant
to restore the person to faith. In this verse the parallelism suggests
that the physical punishment frightened those who saw it, even close
friends and relatives.

Therefore, in coming to a choice, several items are in play.

- What physical manifestation?

- Why the manifestation?

- Why the response from others close by?

- Is it figurative or literal?

verses.zh: 那寻索我命的设下网罗；那想要害我的口出恶言，终日思想诡计。
verses.en: Those who seek my life try to entrap me;[NOTE:1] those who want to harm me speak destructive words.All day long they say deceitful things.
notes: Heb “and the ones near me off at a distance stand.”

verses.zh: 但我如聋子不听，像哑巴不开口。
verses.en: But I am like a deaf man—I hear nothing;I am like a mute who cannot speak.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “lay snares.”
verses.commentary:
38:13-22 This strophe has a mixture of
current conditions (sickness, pain, injury) and future hope in YHWH's
mercy.

- current physical problems

- does not hear (i.e., pretends he does not hear their slander), Ps. 38:13; Ps. 39:2,4

- does not speak (i.e., respond to his accusers, cf. Isa. 53:7), Ps. 38:13b

- ready to stumble, Ps. 38:16b-17a; imagery for trouble, cf. Deut. 32:35; God's path
was straight, level, and clear of obstacles (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY)

- sorrow continually before him (his sin weighs heavily on him), Ps. 38:17b; Ps. 51:3

- full of anxiety, Ps. 38:18

- his enemies attack, Ps. 38:16,19-20

- they grow strong and numerous, Ps. 38:19a

- they hate him wrongfully, Ps. 38:19b

- they repay evil for good, Ps. 38:20; Ps. 35:12; 109:5

- they oppose him because he does what is good, Ps. 38:20b

- confidence in YHWH's love, mercy, and forgiveness

- hope (lit. "wait," BDB 403, KB 407, Hiphil perfect)
in YHWH, Ps. 38:15a, cf. Job 13:15; Ps. 31:24; 33:22; 39:7; 42:5,11; 43:5

- confident YHWH will answer his prayer, Ps. 38:15b

- confident his enemies will not succeed and gloat over his fall, Ps. 38:16

- he prays (two jussives, one imperative)

(1) do not forsake me – BDB 736, KB 806, Qal imperfect
used in a jussive sense, cf. Ps. 9:10; 71:9,18; 94:14; 119:8; Isa. 49:14

(2) do not be far from me – BDB 934, KB 1221, Qal imperfect
used in a jussive sense, cf. Ps. 22:11,19; 35:22; 71:12

(3) make haste to help me – BDB 301, KB 300, Qal imperative,
cf. Ps. 22:19b; 40:13; 70:1,5; 71:12; 141:1

verses.zh: 我如不听见的人，口中没有回话。
verses.en: I am like a man who cannot hearand is incapable of arguing his defense.[NOTE:1]
notes: I am like a deaf man…like a mute. The psalmist is like a deaf mute; he is incapable of defending himself and is vulnerable to his enemies’ deception (see v. 14).

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我仰望你！主―我的　神啊，你必应允我！
verses.en: Yet[NOTE:1] I wait for you, O Lord!You will respond, O Lord, my God!
notes: Heb “and there is not in his mouth arguments.”

verses.zh: 我曾说：恐怕他们向我夸耀；我失脚的时候，他们向我夸大。
verses.en: I have prayed for deliverance, because otherwise they will gloat over me;[NOTE:1] when my foot slips they will arrogantly taunt me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or perhaps “surely.”

Heb “For I said, ‘Lest they rejoice over me.’” The psalmist recalls the motivating argument of his petition. He probably prefaced this statement with a prayer for deliverance (see Pss 7:1-2; 13:3-4; 28:1).

verses.zh: 我几乎跌倒；我的痛苦常在我面前。
verses.en: For I am about to stumble,and I am in constant pain.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “they will magnify against me.” See Pss 35:26; 55:13.

verses.zh: 我要承认我的罪孽；我要因我的罪忧愁。
verses.en: Yes,[NOTE:1] I confess my wrongdoing,and I am concerned about my sins.
notes: Heb “and my pain [is] before me continually.”
verses.commentary:
38:18 This is the theological key to this Psalm (cf. Ps. 32:5). Confession brings

- forgiveness from YHWH (cf. Psalm 51; note 1 John 1:9-2:1)

- forgiveness for self

- a sense of restoration of fellowship

Confession recognizes (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: CONFESSION/PROFESSION)

- human guilt for breaking YHWH's laws

- YHWH's character of forgiveness and mercy

verses.zh: 但我的仇敌又活泼又强壮，无理恨我的增多了。
verses.en: But those who are my enemies for no reason are numerous;[NOTE:1] those who hate me without cause outnumber me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “for.” The translation assumes that כִּי (ki) is asseverative here.

Heb “and my enemies, life, are many.” The noun חַיִּים (khayyim, “life”) fits very awkwardly here. The translation assumes an emendation to חִנָּם (khinnam, “without reason”; note the parallelism with שֶׁקֶר [sheqer, “falsely”] and see Pss 35:19; 69:4; Lam 3:52). The verb עָצַם (ʿatsam) can sometimes mean “are strong,” but here it probably focuses on numerical superiority (note the parallel verb רָבַב, ravav, “be many”).

38:19

NASB, NKJV
"vigorous"

NRSV, NJB, REB
"without cause"

TEV
"healthy"

NET Bible
"for no reason"

The MT has "living" (חיים, BDB 313), but
several English translations emend the root to חנם, BDB
336, cf. Ps. 35:19; 69:4. This fits the parallelism of the next line,
"who hate me wrongfully" (BDB 1055).

verses.zh: 以恶报善的与我作对，因我是追求良善。
verses.en: They repay me evil for the good I have done;though I have tried to do good to them, they hurl accusations at me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “are many.”
verses.commentary:
38:20 "those who repay evil for good" This is a recurrent characteristic of sinners
(cf. Ps. 35:12; 38:20; 109:5; Jer. 18:20). The fall has damaged the very inner being of YHWH's
special creatures.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

▣ There is a Hebrew word that follows this phrase in the MT which has a
possible alternative.

- MT, "living," חיים (BDB 313, KB 307)

- LXX, RSV, NEB, "without cause," חנם (BDB 336, KB 334), which fits the
parallelism best

The UBS Text Project, p. 227, gives option #3 an "A" rating. But, it is not translated by
most English translations.

▣ "those who oppose me" This is the
Hebrew root (BDB 966) from which we get the term "satan."

SPECIAL TOPIC: SATAN

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means
that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of
us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are
priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the
major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Does YHWH punish His sinful followers in this life (Ps. 38:2-3)?

- Is Ps. 38:4 a confession of many sins or a literary way of asserting the sinfulness of all humans?

- List the physical problems associated with unconfessed sin.

- Define the word "plague" in Ps. 38:11. Does your definition explain others' reactions to him?

- How is the imagery of "foot slip" related to a life of sin?

- Why is Ps. 38:18 so important?

PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means
that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of
us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are
priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3).
Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has
one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This Psalm has much in common with Psalms 32 and 51.

- In Jewish thought sin and sickness were related (cf. John 9:2; James 5:13-14). Confession
of sin brought answered prayer and restoration of mind, spirit, and body.

When one looks at all the physical problems mentioned, there are too many to be
characteristic of one disease. Probably they are figurative (cf. Isa. 1:5-6; Ps. 103:3). If so,
the focus of the Psalm is not physical healing but forgiveness of sin!

- As in so many Psalms the connection between

- the physical problems

- the attack of enemies

- the rejection of friends

is uncertain. They are all related but how is a mystery. Are they literal or figurative of sin's social consequences?
